:::{#sol-complementary-subspaces-practice}

If $a\,(1, 0) = b\,(1, 1)$,
then $(a, 0) = (b, b)$,
so $b = 0$ and then $a = 0$.
So $\mathcal{S}_1 \cap \mathcal{S}_2 = \cb{\vzero}$.
Any $(x, y) \in \reals^2$ is $(x - y)\,(1, 0) + y\,(1, 1)$,
so $\mathcal{S}_1 + \mathcal{S}_2 = \reals^2$.
Both conditions hold,
so $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ are [complementary](#def-complementary-subspaces) in $\reals^2$.

:::
